declared.title: Effectiveness of error management training: A meta-analysis.
declared.foundIn: Crossref search « effectiveness of error management training a meta-analysis » (2026-11-23); line of research named in the idea scout's notes

population: 24 training studies (N = 2,183) comparing error management training with error-avoidant or exploratory training

findings.text: Across 24 studies, training that encourages making errors and learning from them did better on average than either error-avoidant training or exploration without error encouragement

support.sentence: Although the mean effect of EMT across all 24 identified studies (N = 2,183) was positive and significant (Cohen's d = 0.44), there were several moderators.

findings.text: The gain was larger after training, when the skill had to be used on new tasks, than during training

support.sentence: Moderator analyses showed effect sizes to be larger (a) for posttraining transfer (d = 0.56) than for within-training performance and (b) for performance tasks that were structurally distinct (adaptive transfer; d = 0.80) than for tasks that were similar to training (analogical transfer).

findings.text: The gain was largest on tasks unlike those of the training

support.sentence: Moderator analyses showed effect sizes to be larger (a) for posttraining transfer (d = 0.56) than for within-training performance and (b) for performance tasks that were structurally distinct (adaptive transfer; d = 0.80) than for tasks that were similar to training (analogical transfer).

findings.text: The authors conclude that error management training may suit transfer to new tasks better than error-avoidant training

support.sentence: Results suggest that EMT may be better suited than error-avoidant training methods for promotion of transfer to novel tasks.

limits: errors made on purpose in a training, with guidance: not failures in life
24 studies with wide variation in effects; no confidence interval nor bias correction in the abstract
2008: no later meta-analysis of error management training found (writer and counter-evidence review); later trials are mixed
Loh 2012 (randomized, 164 trainees): error encouragement beat error avoidance but not a neutral training; part of the gain may be the harm of error avoidance
tasks and countries not given in the abstract (full text not read)
allegiance: Frese developed error management training and both authors promote it
